title: Hydride: A Retargetable and Extensible Synthesis-based Compiler for Modern Hardware Architectures
problem: Modern hardware architectures increasingly support diverse and complex instruction sets for image processing and deep learning, but compilers lack automatic retargeting mechanisms to support emerging ISAs. Manually designing IR abstractions and instruction selection for each architecture is time-consuming and difficult to scale.
motivation: Automatic compiler support for diverse hardware architectures is essential to leverage performance features of modern CPUs and accelerators without manual reimplementation.
method: Hydride uses vendor-defined pseudocode specifications to automatically synthesize AutoLLVM IR, an extensible formally-defined intermediate representation that represents instructions across multiple ISAs. It automatically generates instruction selection passes to lower AutoLLVM IR to each target architecture. The system includes a code synthesizer that takes formal semantics of schedule-based languages like Halide and automatically generates optimal code generation.
key_novelty: Automatically synthesizing retargetable compiler infrastructure including IR instructions and instruction selection passes from vendor-defined pseudocode specifications rather than implementing them manually for each architecture.
contributions: AutoLLVM IR: extensible formally-defined intermediate representation representing 3,557 instructions from x86, Hexagon, and ARM using only 397 AutoLLVM instructions
Automatic synthesis of instruction selection passes from ISA pseudocode specifications
Automatic code synthesizer for schedule-based languages generating optimal AutoLLVM IR from formal semantics
New Halide compiler implementation achieving 8-12% speedup on x86 and 3-26% on other targets versus production compilers

metrics.speedup: 8% over production Halide on x86, 3% on ARM, 12% over LLVM backend on x86, 100% on HVX, 26% on ARM

limitations: Not discussed; paper does not address whether the synthesis approach generalizes to non-schedule-based languages or ISAs lacking formal pseudocode specifications.
primary_theme: Automated retargeting via synthesis from ISA specifications
